summary: The milestone completed 4 experiments in 1.3 minutes, including 2 compute-bound experiments. The 1.08-minute independent constraint-saturation audit was the longest compute task, followed by the 0.18-minute V568 evidence contract, but no phase data explains either duration and the locked compute-task GPU-idle indicator is false.
bottlenecks_identified: Disk-mtime reconstruction ranks the work but supplies no task-phase breakdown, so the cause of the 1.08-minute audit tail is not observable.
The GPU snapshot is not task-scoped; with the locked compute-task GPU-idle indicator false, it does not establish accelerator inefficiency during the compute-bound experiments.
No model-count or runner-selection data is available, so a missed DualGPURunner engagement cannot be diagnosed.
improvements_suggested: Emit monotonic start, stop, and phase timers for each experiment instead of relying only on disk-mtime reconstruction.
Attach task-window per-GPU utilization samples to every compute-bound experiment receipt.
Record loaded-model count and selected runner; choose DualGPURunner when 2 or more models are intentionally loaded in parallel, while retaining single-GPU dispatch for single-model work.
Add dependency-aware scheduling to overlap synthesis-only work with active compute work, then measure whether it reduces wall time.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Add experiment phase timers and task-linked GPU telemetry to the conductor receipt path.
Log model cardinality and runner selection, with DualGPURunner dispatch gated on 2 or more parallel models.
Measure dependency-safe overlap of synthesis-only and compute-bound work.
meta_reflection: The main operational limitation was observability, not a demonstrated accelerator bottleneck. No data available this milestone quantifies a time-saving counterfactual or establishes a parallel multi-model task.
